title: 01. Foundations: Prompt Engineering (Deep)
summary: Covers The Anatomy of a Perfect Prompt, Prompting Techniques Compared.
objectives: The Anatomy of a Perfect Prompt

sections.title: The Anatomy of a Perfect Prompt
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│           ANATOMY OF A PRODUCTION AGENT PROMPT                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  A prompt has 5 layers. Each layer serves a specific purpose.

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  LAYER A: ROLE DEFINITION                                    │
  │  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  │
  │  "You are an expert Python developer with 10 years of        │
  │   experience in AI systems and production backends."         │
  │                                                              │
  │  WHY: Sets the persona. LLMs perform better when given       │
  │  a specific expert role. Like asking an expert vs stranger.  │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  LAYER B: CONTEXT / BACKGROUND                               │
  │  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  │
  │  "You are working in a financial services company.           │
  │   The codebase uses Python 3.11, FastAPI, and PostgreSQL."   │
  │                                                              │
  │  WHY: Grounds the LLM in the specific situation.             │
  │  Prevents generic answers that don't fit your use case.      │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  LAYER C: RULES / CONSTRAINTS                                │
  │  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  │
  │  "Rules you MUST follow:                                     │
  │   - Always add type hints to function arguments              │
  │   - Never use global variables                               │
  │   - Add docstrings to every function                         │
  │   - Handle all exceptions explicitly"                        │
  │                                                              │
  │  WHY: Guardrails. Without rules, LLMs do whatever works.    │
  │  With rules, they behave consistently every time.            │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  LAYER D: OUTPUT FORMAT                                      │
  │  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  │
  │  "Always respond in this JSON format:                        │
  │   {                                                          │
  │     'code': 'the python code',                               │
  │     'explanation': 'what it does',                           │
  │     'test_cases': ['test1', 'test2']                         │
  │   }"                                                         │
  │                                                              │
  │  WHY: Structured output = parseable output.                  │
  │  Agents need to process LLM output programmatically.         │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  LAYER E: FEW-SHOT EXAMPLES                                  │
  │  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  │
  │  "Example:                                                   │
  │   Input: 'Add two numbers'                                   │
  │   Output: {                                                  │
  │     'code': 'def add(a: int, b: int) -> int:\n    return a+b'│
  │     'explanation': 'Takes two ints, returns their sum'       │
  │     'test_cases': ['add(2,3)==5', 'add(-1,1)==0']            │
  │   }"                                                         │
  │                                                              │
  │  WHY: Examples are the most powerful way to guide LLMs.      │
  │  "Show don't tell" works for LLMs just like for humans.      │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

sections.title: Prompting Techniques Compared
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│           PROMPT TECHNIQUES — WHEN TO USE WHICH                 │
│                                                                 │
│  1. ZERO-SHOT                                                   │
│  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  │
│  No examples. Just instruction.                                 │
│  "Classify this tweet as positive/negative/neutral: '...'"      │
│  ✅ Use when: task is simple & LLM knows it well                │
│  ❌ Avoid when: specialized format needed                        │
│                                                                 │
│  2. FEW-SHOT                                                    │
│  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  │
│  2-5 examples before the actual task.                           │
│  Tweet: "I love this!" → Positive                               │
│  Tweet: "This sucks"   → Negative                               │
│  Tweet: "It's okay"    → ???                                    │
│  ✅ Use when: specific output format needed                      │
│  ✅ Use when: rare/specialized task                              │
│                                                                 │
│  3. CHAIN-OF-THOUGHT (CoT)                                      │
│  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  │
│  Force step-by-step reasoning.                                  │
│  "Solve this step by step:                                      │
│   Step 1: Identify what we know                                 │
│   Step 2: Apply the formula                                     │
│   Step 3: Calculate..."                                         │
│  ✅ Use when: math, logic, multi-step reasoning                  │
│  ✅ Use when: accuracy matters more than speed                   │
│                                                                 │
│  4. ROLE PROMPTING                                              │
│  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  │
│  Give LLM a specific expert identity.                           │
│  "You are a senior security researcher at Google..."            │
│  ✅ Use when: domain expertise needed                            │
│  ✅ ALWAYS use for agents                                        │
│                                                                 │
│  5. STRUCTURED OUTPUT                                           │
│  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  │
│  Demand JSON/XML/specific format.                               │
│  "Return ONLY valid JSON with fields: name, age, skills"        │
│  ✅ ALWAYS use for agents — they must parse responses           │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
